title: The Spring Scale Bench: What Does Each String Hold?
intro: One spring scale, four rigs. You will calibrate the scale, put it in the string of a moving cart, read the rods of a walkway model, and read the tension between the links of a hanging chain.
introSteps: Read two short cards: what a spring scale reads, and what tension is.
Walk to the scale bench and press E. Part A: hang masses, record the stretch, and find your scale's spring constant.
Part B: put the scale in the string of a cart pulled by a hanging mass. Hold it still, predict, then let go.
Halfway through, the teacher calls a huddle. Eyes up, copy the board.
Part C: read the walkway model in both designs. Part D: read a hanging chain link by link. Each part ends with a check.
keyRows: Walk. On screen you move along the floor diagonals.
Use what you are facing (the scale bench).
Point at anything to see its name.

hook.ask: Two walkways hang one above the other from the same rods. Which nut holds the most?
hook.note: In 1981 a small change to a drawing like this one doubled the load on one nut. By the end of today you will see why.

goal: Goal: read the force in a string, a rod or a chain link, and say what it holds.

cards.body: A spring scale is a spring in a case. Pull on it and the spring stretches: F = kx, where k is the spring constant in newtons per metre and x is the stretch in metres. Once you know k, the stretch tells you the force. Put the scale anywhere in a string and it reads the pull in the string at that spot.

Tension is the pull a string, a rope, a rod or a chain link carries. A light string pulls with the same tension along its whole length. A chain with mass does not: each link holds up every link and load below it. To find a tension, draw a free-body diagram of what hangs below that spot.

steps.calib: Part A. Hang three masses, one at a time, and record each stretch. Then find k for your scale.
steps.cp1: Check 1: spring scales. Three right in a row.
steps.string: Part B. Record a reading held still. Then predict, release, and record on two different setups.
steps.cp2: Check 2: the string. Three right in a row.
steps.hyatt: Part C. Record the walkway model in both designs, then answer the question.
steps.chain: Part D. Read three gaps in the chain, predict the top, then read the top.
steps.cp3: Check 3: what each piece holds. Three right in a row.
steps.done: Done. Hand in, then take out your paper worksheet.

hyatt.story: This is what happened at the Hyatt Regency hotel in Kansas City on July 17, 1981. The walkways were drawn with one long rod. The builder changed it to two rods, which was easier to make. The rods were fine; the nut under the fourth-floor walkway's beam now held both walkways. It pulled through the beam, both walkways fell, and 114 people died.

demo: Welcome. This tour shows every control. None of it counts toward your lab.
Walk with the arrow keys or WASD. Press E at the scale bench, the long bench with the hanging scale.
Part A: click a mass to hang it. The ruler shows the stretch. Press Record for each mass.
With three rows in the table, work out k from your own readings and type it in. Then a check: three right in a row.
Part B: the scale is in the string between the cart and the pulley. Held still, it reads the weight of the hanging mass. Before you let go, predict.
Release. Both masses speed up together, and the scale reads less than it did held. Record it, then try another setup.
Part C: the walkway model. Switch between the design on paper and the design as built, and read the rods and the circled nut.
Part D: click a gap in the chain to move the scale there. Lower gaps hold less. Predict the top before you read it.
Stuck? The help button locks your screen until the teacher comes. So do three misses in a row on a check. Your teacher types a code to open it.
That is the whole bench. Press Esc to close it. Your lab starts when the tour ends.

ui.kYes: Right: k = {k} N/m. Your scale now reads in newtons.
ui.kSay: The scale is calibrated. It reads in newtons now.
ui.kHint_cm: Check the units of the stretch: k is in newtons per metre, so the stretch goes in metres.
ui.kHint_mass: The spring is stretched by a force. Use the weight column, not the mass.
ui.kHint_flip: You divided the wrong way. k is the force divided by the stretch.
ui.kHint_rows: Pick one row. Divide its weight by its stretch in metres. Do another row to check.
ui.recSame: That mass is already in the table. Try another one.
ui.recRelease: Release the cart first, then Record while it moves.

ui.cMore: Record both designs to go on.

ui.cpQ_findK: A spring scale stretches {x} cm when a {m} kg mass hangs still on it. What is its spring constant?
ui.cpQ_findF: A spring scale with k = {k} N/m is stretched {x} cm. What does it read?
ui.cpQ_held: A {M} kg cart sits on a frictionless table. A string runs from the cart over a pulley to a {m} kg hanging mass, with a spring scale in the string. You hold the cart still. What does the scale read?
ui.cpQ_released: A {M} kg cart sits on a frictionless table. A string runs from the cart over a pulley to a {m} kg hanging mass, with a spring scale in the string. You let go and both speed up. What does the scale read while they move?
ui.cpQ_chain: A chain of {N} links hangs from the ceiling. Each link has a mass of {mL} kg, and a {B} kg bucket hangs from the bottom link. What is the tension just above link {j}, counting links from the bottom?
ui.cpQ_chain0: A chain of {N} links hangs from the ceiling. Each link has a mass of {mL} kg, and nothing hangs from the bottom link. What is the tension just above link {j}, counting links from the bottom?
ui.cpQ_walk: Two walkways hang one above the other from the same rods. On one rod, the upper walkway's load is {up} N and the lower walkway's is {low} N. {where} What force does it hold?

ui.cpWhere_nut1: As designed, one long rod runs from the ceiling to the lower walkway, and each walkway sits on its own nut. Look at the nut under the upper walkway.
ui.cpWhere_upper: Look at the rod between the ceiling and the upper walkway.
ui.cpWhere_lower: Look at the rod between the two walkways.
ui.cpPass: Passed. On to the next part.
ui.cpHint_cm: Check the stretch's units. k is in newtons per metre, so the stretch goes in metres.
ui.cpHint_mass: Turn the mass into its weight first.
ui.cpHint_springK: The force on the scale is the hanging weight. Divide it by the stretch in metres.
ui.cpHint_springF: The reading is the spring's force: k times the stretch in metres.
ui.cpHint_held: That is the held reading. Once released, the hanging mass speeds up, so the string pulls up on it with less than its weight.
ui.cpHint_still: Nothing moves here. The hanging mass is in equilibrium, so the string holds all of its weight.
ui.cpHint_accel: That number is the acceleration. The tension is the force that speeds up the cart.
ui.cpHint_cart: The table holds up the cart's weight, not the string. The string only speeds the cart up.
ui.cpHint_string: Draw a free-body diagram of the cart. The only sideways force on it is the string.
ui.cpHint_whole: That is the load at the very top. This point holds only what hangs below it.
ui.cpHint_bucket: Something else hangs below that point too.
ui.cpHint_count: Count the links below that point again. Link 1 is the bottom link.
ui.cpHint_below: Find everything that hangs below that point and add up its weight.
ui.cpHint_own: As built, the lower rod hangs from that same beam, so the nut holds more than its own walkway.
